titleText.es: El extraño sentido del deber que tienen los buenos sysadmins bordea lo sociopático, pero está bien saber que se interpone entre las fuerzas de la oscuridad y los servidores del blog de tu gato.
titleText.en: The weird sense of duty really good sysadmins have can border on the sociopathic, but it's nice to know that it stands between the forces of darkness and your cat blog's servers.
titleText.noteEn: The Spanish archive and official xkcd source both identify comic #705, published 2010-02-22, and their title texts are preserved exactly. The Spanish raster integrates the technical loans UPTIME and SYSADMIN into Spanish syntax, so both remain lexical targets. OCR split the printed wraps ASEGURA-/DO, COR-/TADO, COMUNICACIO-/NES, VENTILA-/CIÓN, MUR-/MURANDO, and TRATA-/MOS; misread IGNORÓ as INGORÓ and the second part of MURMURANDO as ELRANDO; and entirely omitted the separate EL and quoted UPTIME line. The authored transcript follows the visible raster rather than those OCR errors.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Capturado is the completed-action form of capturar. After a form of haber, it describes the completed act of capturing someone or something.

example.en: They have captured the fugitive.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Rehenes is the plural of rehén, a person held so that another person or group will meet a demand.

example.en: The hostages came out safely.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Asegurado is the completed-action form of asegurar. In a security context it can mean bringing a place under control or making it safe.

example.es: El equipo ha asegurado la entrada.
example.en: The team has secured the entrance.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Cortado is the completed-action form of cortar. With a service, signal, or communication link, it means that the connection has been interrupted.

example.es: Han cortado la conexión durante la reparación.
example.en: They have cut off the connection during the repair.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Comunicaciones can refer collectively to the systems or channels used to exchange messages and information.

example.en: The storm damaged the communications systems.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Excelente can describe something of very high quality or stand alone as a positive reaction to news or a result.

example.en: ‘It is ready now.’ ‘Excellent!’

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Trepó is the completed-past form of trepar for one person or thing. It presents the climb as a finished event.

example.es: El gato trepó por el árbol.
example.en: The cat climbed up the tree.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: A conducto is an enclosed channel through which air, liquid, cables, or another material can pass. Conductos is plural.

example.es: El aire circula por los conductos.
example.en: The air circulates through the ducts.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Ventilación is the movement or replacement of air in an enclosed space.

example.en: The room needs better ventilation.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Atravesó is the completed-past form of atravesar for one person or thing. It describes movement from one side of something to the other.

example.en: The runner crossed the park.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Cristal can mean glass as a material or one pane or panel of glass. Cristales is plural.

example.es: Cambiaron los cristales de las ventanas.
example.en: They replaced the window panes.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Rotos is the masculine plural form of roto. It matches a masculine plural noun describing things that have broken.

example.en: They removed the broken plates.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Matando is the -ando form of matar. It can add an action that happens at the same time as another action.

example.es: El veneno avanzó, matando a los insectos.
example.en: The poison spread, killing the insects.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Enviamos can be present or completed past. A narrative of finished events gives it the completed-past reading.

example.en: Yesterday we sent two technicians.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Detener stays in its unchanged -er form and le is attached to represent a male person. This use of le for a singular male person is common and accepted in Spain; detenerlo is also widely used.

example.es: Mandaron a dos agentes para detenerle.
example.en: They sent two officers to stop him.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Rescatado is the completed-action form of rescatar. After a form of haber, it describes a completed rescue.

example.en: They have rescued the hiker.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Ignoró is the completed-past form of ignorar for one person or thing. The written accent distinguishes this form from present-time ignoro, ‘I ignore.’

example.en: She ignored the warning.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Reconectó is the completed-past form of reconectar for one person or thing. The prefix re- adds the sense of connecting again.

example.en: The technician reconnected the cable.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Murmurando is the -ando form of murmurar. It describes speaking very quietly or indistinctly while another action happens.

example.en: He left muttering a complaint.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: uptime; time a system remains available
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Uptime is an English technical loan used by Spanish-speaking computing professionals for the time that a computer or service stays running and reachable.

example.es: El servidor mantiene un uptime muy alto.
example.en: The server maintains very high uptime.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: we are dealing; we deal (with con)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Tratamos is the present nosotros form of tratar. Followed by con, it can mean dealing with or facing a person, problem, or situation.

example.en: We are dealing with a delicate problem.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Sysadmin is an English computing loan used for the person who maintains computer systems, servers, accounts, and related services. Spanish also uses administrador or administradora de sistemas.

example.en: The system administrator checked the servers.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How can you refer back to something one familiar listener said?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Say como dijiste, meaning ‘as you said.’
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Como introduces the comparison with the earlier words, and dijiste is the completed-past tú form of decir. Other people require a different form: como dije, como dijo, como dijimos.

example.en: I did it as you said.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that communication links are cut off?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use a matching form of cortar followed by las comunicaciones.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Cortar changes for the person and time. Las comunicaciones names the channels or systems that are interrupted.

example.en: The failure cut off communications.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that someone climbs through, along, or up a route or surface?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use a matching form of trepar, then por, then name the route or surface.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Trepar changes for the person and time. Por introduces the path used for the climb.

example.es: Trepamos por la pared de roca.
example.en: We climbed up the rock wall.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: What is a common Spanish expression for a ventilation duct?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Say conducto de ventilación; use conductos de ventilación in the plural.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Conducto names the passage, while de ventilación identifies its function. Ventilación stays singular after de.

example.en: They cleaned the ventilation ducts.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that someone quietly mutters something about a topic?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use a matching form of murmurar, optionally add algo, then use sobre before the topic.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Murmurar changes for the person and time. Sobre introduces what the quiet remark concerns.

example.en: She muttered something about the schedule.

cardDefinitions.promptEs: tratar con + persona, problema o situación
cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that someone deals with or faces a person, problem, or situation?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use a matching form of tratar followed by con and the person or thing.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Tratar changes for the person and time, while con stays unchanged before what is being dealt with.

example.es: La directora trata con muchos proveedores.
example.en: The director deals with many suppliers.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: A system administrator maintains services and may care intensely about uptime, the time those services remain available.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The joke makes that professional duty absurdly dominant: the intruder ignores hostages and danger, restores the cut cables, and is recognized as a sysadmin because he prioritizes uptime above the ostensible rescue mission.

applications.explanationEn: Trepó supplies the completed climb, por introduces its route, and los conductos de ventilación fills that route slot.
Conductos names the passages, and de ventilación identifies their function while ventilación remains singular.
Rotos follows cristales in the common neutral order for a descriptive adjective.
Rotos uses masculine plural -os to match masculine plural cristales.
Matando adds an action happening alongside the movement through the broken glass.
A marks the defined group of people as the direct object, and todos los que enviamos supplies that complete group.
Todos los identifies an understood group of people, and que introduces the action enviamos that defines them.
Los identifies an unnamed masculine or mixed group, que introduces what defines that group, and enviamos supplies the defining action.
Para introduces the purpose, and detenerle keeps detener in its unchanged -er form with the person word attached.
Le is written on the end of the unchanged verb detener as one word.
Trepó presents the climb as one bounded completed event.
Atravesó presents the crossing as one bounded completed event.
Enviamos presents the dispatch of other people as a completed event in the report.
